I'd give this game a solid 7/10. It is my first Monster Hunter game and I like the boss fights, though a little repetitive they are all unique and fun. the weapon upgrade system takes a little getting used to, and crafting  and obtaining items isn't always the most straightforward. But that's just the opinion of a casual.
It's challenging in a good way and it's worth it.

Here's the part they don't tell you. Halfway through the game, a "special" monster starts following you around. Between areas, across the different mission modes, everywhere. This monster, Bazelgeuse, will be drawn to the sound of you fighting monsters, and will carpet your battlefield with bombs. These will damage you heavily, even with heavy armor, chain you into other ones, and light you on fire, which you then have to sheathe your weapon mid-combat and roll; or dodge repeatedly to put out, all while Bazelgeuse and what you're fighting suddenly stop fighting each other and begin attacking you. It's possible alone, probably, but later on, you will want to bring a team, unless you relish a half hour of fighting a boss enemy (true story!) Also, the DLC is an obvious scam, adding only a handful of new areas and effectively paywalling a tool that a lot of established players will insist is a necessity and a convenience, all at 2/3 the base game's price. What a bargain!
Get it on sale or don't get it.

Monster Hunter: World – 1,503 Hours Well Spent

Monster Hunter: World was a huge turning point for the series. It brought Monster Hunter into a new era with modern graphics, a living and breathing ecosystem, seamless environments, and a much more accessible multiplayer experience. It also helped bring the series to a much wider audience around the world.

I've spent over 1,503 hours playing this game, and honestly, I don't regret a single hour.

What makes this game special is that even after almost nine years, it still has an active player base. I think that's a testament to just how good this game is. Not many games can keep players coming back for so many years.

I also love the story and its memorable cutscenes. And the soundtrack deserves special mention. Some of the songs are genuinely touching and make certain moments in the game even more memorable.

Monster Hunter: World isn't just a game I enjoyed playing; it's one of those games that leaves a lasting impression.

1,503 hours later, I'd still happily recommend it to anyone who wants to experience Monster Hunter.
